answer: Each identity opens a segregated reserve entry on the terrace board locking 50 plus 20 percent on a 100 claim. The kernel ledger lists each account and claim barring double-counting. Yarrow auditors recompute ratios from the kernel ledger; a shortfall freezes payout and burns the reserve. The kth identity pays a 2(k-1) segregation fee, with its entry checked against all prior ones. The 1000th fake costs 2068, and 1000 fakes cost 1,069,000. A reserve-sharing ring fails when yarrow auditors spot shared credit on two accounts and burn both. An honest identity locks 70, recovered on settlement.
